page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7a.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.55 GHz. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and its network configuration provides a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct performance profile. The instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance is weak, falling into the bottom 25% for stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core tests. Memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck; read-only and write large-block tests register in the bottom 10%, indicating poor uncached memory throughput. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression show average performance, whereas multi-threaded decompression and database operations score in the lower percentiles.

Given the high memory density relative to the vCPU count, this instance is designed for memory-bound workloads that do not require high-throughput parallel processing or local disk storage. It is suitable for caching layers, small-scale in-memory databases, and lightweight text or web-serving applications that benefit from a larger memory footprint. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a low-cost entry point for memory-intensive applications, though users must weigh the generous RAM allocation against the lower multi-core and memory bandwidth performance.
